blocks.text: Dohra:
A number of Khalsa Singhs joined Kaura Mai, As they considered him a devout Sikh of the Guru. Thus did Kaura Mai attack Shah Nawaz2 , Being assured of the Khalsa Singh's support. (1)
lines: A number of Khalsa Singhs joined Kaura Mai,
As they considered him a devout Sikh of the Guru.
Thus did Kaura Mai attack Shah Nawaz2 ,
Being assured of the Khalsa Singh's support.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Wherever the Khalsa Panth organized a congregation, Dewan Kaura Mai did join the morning prayers everyday. Regularly would he listen to the morning and evening prayers, Daily would he make an offering of provisions to the Khalsa Panth. (2)
lines: Wherever the Khalsa Panth organized a congregation,
Dewan Kaura Mai did join the morning prayers everyday.
Regularly would he listen to the morning and evening prayers,
Daily would he make an offering of provisions to the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Daily would he sit among the Singhs after a due permission, Gladly would he exchange the Khalsa Panth's greetings. Daily would he offer provisions to the community kitchen, Making an offering of five rupees to each Nihang chief. (3)
lines: Daily would he sit among the Singhs after a due permission,
Gladly would he exchange the Khalsa Panth's greetings.
Daily would he offer provisions to the community kitchen,
Making an offering of five rupees to each Nihang chief.

blocks.text: Gladly would he pay a penalty of five rupees, For getting permission for smoking a pipe. Surely would he be able to arrest Shah Nawaz, Claiming to be having blessings of the Divine Guru. (4)
lines: Gladly would he pay a penalty of five rupees,
For getting permission for smoking a pipe.
Surely would he be able to arrest Shah Nawaz,
Claiming to be having blessings of the Divine Guru.

blocks.text: Instantly, did the Khalsa contradict his claim, As the Khalsa would fain to eliminate him altogether. As he had got innumerable number of Singhs slaughtered, How could they spare his life once he came in their sight. (5)
lines: Instantly, did the Khalsa contradict his claim,
As the Khalsa would fain to eliminate him altogether.
As he had got innumerable number of Singhs slaughtered,
How could they spare his life once he came in their sight.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Putting more Mughal troops under Kaura Mai's command, Shah Nawaz's real brother, too, was sent with him. Putting the latter under Kaura Mai's command forcibly, Was this force despatched towards Shah Nawaz's camp. (6)
lines: Putting more Mughal troops under Kaura Mai's command,
Shah Nawaz's real brother, too, was sent with him.
Putting the latter under Kaura Mai's command forcibly,
Was this force despatched towards Shah Nawaz's camp.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

While Shah Nawaz was the custodian of Lahore, Had he looted, oppressed and slaughtered so many people. It was for these atrocities that Mir Mannu3 sent this force, To join the forces under the command of Dewan Kaura Mai. (7)
lines: While Shah Nawaz was the custodian of Lahore,
Had he looted, oppressed and slaughtered so many people.
It was for these atrocities that Mir Mannu3 sent this force,
To join the forces under the command of Dewan Kaura Mai.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the battle raged between both the forces, Both the armies were expecting to win the battle. Both Shah Nawaz and Kaura Mai being (mighty) warriors, Stood facing each other in the field of battle. (8)
lines: As the battle raged between both the forces,
Both the armies were expecting to win the battle.
Both Shah Nawaz and Kaura Mai being (mighty) warriors,
Stood facing each other in the field of battle.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Mughal troops from both sides having become allies, They wished the Hindu Dewan Kaura Mai slaughtered. Upon this, reposing complete faith in the Divine Guru, Kaura Mai positioned the Singh soldiers around him. (9)
lines: The Mughal troops from both sides having become allies,
They wished the Hindu Dewan Kaura Mai slaughtered.
Upon this, reposing complete faith in the Divine Guru,
Kaura Mai positioned the Singh soldiers around him.

blocks.text: As Shah Nawaz mounted a forceful attack, He moved his horse to stand in front of Kaura Mai. Kaura Mai beckoned the Khalsa to avail of that opportunity, As Shah Nawaz was going to attack the former. (10)
lines: As Shah Nawaz mounted a forceful attack,
He moved his horse to stand in front of Kaura Mai.
Kaura Mai beckoned the Khalsa to avail of that opportunity,
As Shah Nawaz was going to attack the former.

blocks.text: Asking Dewan Kaura Mai not to lose heart at all, Must he forewarn the Singhs as the enemy approached, Assuring him of their being in complete readiness, Instantly would they slaughter the enemy as he arrived. (11)
lines: Asking Dewan Kaura Mai not to lose heart at all,
Must he forewarn the Singhs as the enemy approached,
Assuring him of their being in complete readiness,
Instantly would they slaughter the enemy as he arrived.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon, approaching Shah Nawaz accused Kaura Mai, That the latter had been an ungrateful untrue to his salt. He must, therefore, either get ready for a fight, Or else bow down and salute a Mughal ruler. (12)
lines: Thereupon, approaching Shah Nawaz accused Kaura Mai,
That the latter had been an ungrateful untrue to his salt.
He must, therefore, either get ready for a fight,
Or else bow down and salute a Mughal ruler.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this Kaura Mai did inform his Singh supporters, That such abusive words indeed was Shah Nawaz uttering. At this, as the (incensed) Singhs fired their muskets, Did a bullet hit right into Shah Nawaz's heart. (13)
lines: At this Kaura Mai did inform his Singh supporters,
That such abusive words indeed was Shah Nawaz uttering.
At this, as the (incensed) Singhs fired their muskets,
Did a bullet hit right into Shah Nawaz's heart.

blocks.text: With a bound did he fall from his horse, As he could not stand up after being hit by a bullet. Thereafter, a Singh after getting down from his horse, Picked up his head after beheading Shah Nawaz. (14)
lines: With a bound did he fall from his horse,
As he could not stand up after being hit by a bullet.
Thereafter, a Singh after getting down from his horse,
Picked up his head after beheading Shah Nawaz.

blocks.text: As his severed head was presented before Mir Mannu, Delighted did he feel at the sight of his beheaded enemy. Picking up a pen and a paper did Mir Mannu confer, The title of 'Bahadur' on Kaura Mai in writing. (15)
lines: As his severed head was presented before Mir Mannu,
Delighted did he feel at the sight of his beheaded enemy.
Picking up a pen and a paper did Mir Mannu confer,
The title of 'Bahadur' on Kaura Mai in writing.

blocks.text: The noble service that Kaura Mai had rendered unto the Khalsa, Was indeed rewarded immediately (by the Divine Guru). Listen further to the episodes (dear readers), As were these narrated by the author's ancestors. (16)
lines: The noble service that Kaura Mai had rendered unto the Khalsa,
Was indeed rewarded immediately (by the Divine Guru).
Listen further to the episodes (dear readers),
As were these narrated by the author's ancestors.

blocks.text: Dohra:
It was in the year of eighteen hundred and six, That Shah Nawaz did shed his mortal frame. The way Rattan Singh (the author) had heard the account, Had he narrated it in the same manner. (17)
lines: It was in the year of eighteen hundred and six,
That Shah Nawaz did shed his mortal frame.
The way Rattan Singh (the author) had heard the account,
Had he narrated it in the same manner.
